title: Prototype Pollution in csvjson via toSchemaObject headers
longFix: `toSchemaObject` builds nested objects from CSV header names via `addDataInSchema` with no guard on reserved keys; a header like `__proto__.x` or `constructor.prototype.x` mutated Object.prototype. Headers whose dotted/bracketed segments name a prototype slot are now rejected.
summary: `csvjson.toSchemaObject()` interprets dotted/bracketed CSV column headers (e.g. `name.first`) to build nested objects. With no guard on reserved property names, a header such as `__proto__.polluted` or `constructor.prototype.polluted` causes the schema builder to walk into and mutate `Object.prototype`, affecting every object in the process (the `__proto__[]` variant instead throws, a denial-of-service). The attacker only needs to control the header row of a parsed CSV.
fixExplanation: `addDataInSchema` now splits each header on `.`, `[`, and `]` and rejects the header if any segment is `__proto__`, `constructor`, or `prototype`. Legitimate nested headers — and headers that merely contain those words as substrings, e.g. `constructorName` — are unaffected.
